question: ENIAC, the first electronics digital programmable computer device (1943), stands for ________.

options.text: Electronic Numerical Integrator and Analytical Computer

solution:
Source Code:

The correct answer is __**Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **ENIAC** stands for **Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer**.
 
• ENIAC was the first electronic digital programmable computer device developed in the year **1943**.
 
• It was designed and built by **John W. Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert** at the University of Pennsylvania.
 
• ENIAC was capable of performing complex calculations much faster than any prior human or mechanical computing methods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of ENIAC**

 
 
• ENIAC, short for Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer, was a groundbreaking machine in the history of computing.
 
• It was developed during World War II and was primarily used for calculating artillery firing tables for the United States Army's Ballistic Research Laboratory.
 
• ENIAC's development began in 1943 and was completed in 1945. It was unveiled to the public in 1946.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications of ENIAC**
 
 
• ENIAC was composed of 17,468 vacuum tubes, 7,200 crystal diodes, 1,500 relays, 70,000 resistors, and 10,000 capacitors.
 
• The machine consumed about 150 kilowatts of electrical power and could perform around 5,000 additions per second.
 
• ENIAC was reprogrammable, which meant it could be reconfigured to solve different types of problems, albeit through manual rewiring and setting of switches.
 
 
 
• **Impact and Legacy of ENIAC**
 
 
• ENIAC demonstrated the feasibility and potential of electronic digital computing, paving the way for future advancements in computer science and technology.
 
• The concepts and technologies developed for ENIAC influenced subsequent computer designs and contributed to the evolution of modern computers.
 
• ENIAC's success also spurred interest and investment in further research and development of electronic computing systems.
 
 
 
• **Key Figures in ENIAC's Development**
 
 
• John W. Mauchly and J. Presper Eckert were the primary designers and engineers behind ENIAC.
 
• They collaborated with a team of engineers, including women mathematicians known as "computers," who played an essential role in programming and operating ENIAC.
 
• After the success of ENIAC, Mauchly and Eckert continued to make significant contributions to the field of computing, including the development of the UNIVAC I, one of the first commercially available computers.
